target.title: fix(lobster): don't route schema-default flowExpectedRevision into TaskFlow (#102011)
target.body:
Closes #102011

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ordinary `@openclaw/lobster` tool `run` / `resume` calls fail
by being misrouted into managed TaskFlow mode. When the tool schema supplies a
default `flowExpectedRevision` (e.g. `0`) for a minimal call, the wrapper treated
that always-present value as a managed-flow signal — so an ordinary `resume`
(token + approve, no `flowId`) errored with `flowId required when using managed
TaskFlow resume mode`, and a managed `run` could be rejected with `run action
does not accept flowId or flowExpectedRevision`. The standalone Lobster CLI
handled the same workflow correctly, confirming the fault is in the OpenClaw
plugin wrapper's schema/param interaction.

## Why This Change Was Made

Managed TaskFlow mode is identified by its flow identifier — `flowId` for
`resume`, `flowControllerId`/`flowGoal` for `run` — not by the secondary
`flowExpectedRevision`, which the tool schema can inject as a default. The fix
routes `resume` to managed mode only when `flowId` is present, and stops `run`
from rejecting a schema-injected `flowExpectedRevision` (it now rejects only an
explicit `flowId`). Real managed flows are unchanged: managed `resume` still
requires `flowExpectedRevision`, and managed `run` still needs
`flowControllerId`/`flowGoal`.

## User Impact

The documented minimal `run` / `resume` Lobster tool calls work again; ordinary
approval workflows no longer fail with a spurious managed-TaskFlow error.

## Evidence

Two regression tests added in `extensions/lobster/src/lobster-tool.test.ts`:
- An ordinary `resume` carrying only a schema-default `flowExpectedRevision: 0`
  (no `flowId`) now runs as an ordinary resume (`taskFlow.resume` not called,
  `runner.run` invoked) instead of erroring.
- A managed `run` with an injected `flowExpectedRevision: 0` is accepted
  (`taskFlow.createManaged` called) instead of being rejected.

Real behavior proof — the two new tests drive the actual `createLobsterTool`
tool. Before the patch they fail with the exact reported errors (`flowId
required…` / `run action does not accept flowId or flowExpectedRevision`); after
the patch the full suite passes (19 tests) via
`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/lobster/src/lobster-tool.test.ts`.
oxfmt/oxlint clean. Reproduced the before/after by toggling the source with
`git stash` while keeping the new tests.

---

AI-assisted: written with Claude Code. The before/after evidence is from running
the real tool locally, not AI-generated assertions taken on faith.
